title: Keep cancel-in-progress false on PR-scoped workflows that mutate state mid-run
answers: team-review label added but reviewers never assigned
cancelling a bot workflow strands routing
why cancel-in-progress is false in workflow concurrency
body:
Symptom: A PR gets the team-review label but no reviewers are assigned, and no label-added follow-up fires.
Root cause: .github/workflows/route-ready-issue-pr.yml runs route-ready-issue-pr.js, which adds the team-review label with GITHUB_TOKEN and then runs runTeamReview. Cancelling the run between those two steps leaves the label in place. A replacement run whose payload already has the label exits early, and GITHUB_TOKEN label writes do not emit a new label event.
Fix pattern: Set `cancel-in-progress: false` in the concurrency block of every workflow that the PR-scoped group covers, so an in-flight run always finishes. The group still coalesces pending runs.
Constraints: cancel-in-progress only protects a running run; a pending run in the same group is still replaced by a later event. Cancelling is acceptable only for idempotent, low-cost jobs, as the PR argued for the ubuntu-slim gated workflows.
applies: Any workflow with a concurrency group that performs non-idempotent side effects such as label writes or review requests, and that could be superseded mid-run.
says: Pull requests get marked for team review but reviewers are never assigned.
Automated pull request review assignment stops when subsequent commits cancel running workflows.
Pull requests remain stranded with review labels without notifying any team members.
Review routing bot adds the label but never requests reviews on updated pull requests.
Prevent new code pushes from interrupting automated reviewer assignment on open pull requests.
search: Workflows with concurrency groups that perform non-idempotent side effects must set cancel-in-progress: false so in-flight runs are not cancelled mid-execution. In .github/workflows/route-ready-issue-pr.yml, cancelling route-ready-issue-pr.js between adding the team-review label and running runTeamReview strands the PR without assigned reviewers. While cancel-in-progress: false protects active runs, pending runs are still coalesced, and cancelling remains acceptable only for low-cost idempotent jobs.
